cameras.name: iPhone 17 Pro

codecs.name: ProRes 422 HQ
codecs.ref: Apple ProRes White Paper (April 2022), target data rate ProRes 422 HQ 1920x1080 29.97p = 220 Mb/s (bpp = Mbps*1e6/(1920*1080*29.97)). Native Camera app records ProRes 422 HQ (flavor not named on apple.com; confirmed by third-party sources and consistent with Apple's external-drive write-speed requirements). iPhone ProRes limits (Apple support 109041): built-in storage 4K up to 30 fps (256 GB+), 1080p up to 60 fps (25/30 only on 128 GB); 4K60 requires external SSD >=220 MB/s, 4K120 requires external SSD >=440 MB/s. Apple's 220/440 MB/s requirements match 422 HQ 4K at ~1768/~3536 Mb/s.

codecs.name: ProRes 422
codecs.ref: Apple ProRes White Paper (April 2022), target data rate ProRes 422 1920x1080 29.97p = 147 Mb/s (bpp = Mbps*1e6/(1920*1080*29.97)). Only via third-party apps (e.g. Blackmagic Camera); not the native Camera app — third-party info.

codecs.name: ProRes 422 LT
codecs.ref: Apple ProRes White Paper (April 2022), target data rate ProRes 422 LT 1920x1080 29.97p = 102 Mb/s (bpp = Mbps*1e6/(1920*1080*29.97)). Only via third-party apps; third-party info.

codecs.name: ProRes 422 Proxy
codecs.ref: Apple ProRes White Paper (April 2022), target data rate ProRes 422 Proxy 1920x1080 29.97p = 45 Mb/s (bpp = Mbps*1e6/(1920*1080*29.97)). Only via third-party apps; third-party info.

codecs.name: ProRes RAW
codecs.ref: ESTIMATE. Apple ProRes RAW White Paper (May 2023) gives no numeric table, only that ProRes RAW rates 'generally fall between' two ProRes flavors; midpoint of 147 and 220 Mb/s at 1920x1080 29.97 (ProRes WP April 2022) = 183.5 Mb/s. ProRes RAW is constant-quality, so real rates vary with detail/noise. Apple lists ProRes RAW as a recorded format, 'enabled by compatible apps' (Final Cut Camera, third-party). Apple publishes no iPhone ProRes RAW resolution/fps limits; 4K assumed.

codecs.name: ProRes RAW HQ
codecs.ref: ESTIMATE. Apple ProRes RAW White Paper (May 2023) gives no numeric table, only that ProRes RAW HQ rates 'generally fall between' two ProRes flavors; midpoint of 220 and 330 Mb/s at 1920x1080 29.97 (ProRes WP April 2022) = 275.0 Mb/s. ProRes RAW is constant-quality, so real rates vary with detail/noise. Whether RAW vs RAW HQ is selectable depends on app; Apple publishes no iPhone-specific rate.

cameras.notes: Apple tech specs: 4K Dolby Vision at 24/25/30/60 fps, 100/120 fps (Fusion Main camera only); 1080p at 25/30/60/120 fps (120 Fusion Main); slo-mo 1080p up to 240 fps and 4K up to 120 fps; 720p 30 fps; Cinematic mode up to 4K 30 fps; Action mode up to 2.8K 60 fps; spatial 1080p30. 'ProRes video recording up to 4K at 120 fps with external recording.' Formats: HEVC, H.264, ProRes, ProRes RAW. Apple Log 2 and ACES supported; Apple Log 2 is a gamma/encoding curve, not a codec, and does not change ProRes data rates. Genlock with third-party hardware. No 4K DCI, 6K or 8K recording listed.

Released: Apple support tech-spec page 148590 lists 'Year introduced: 2026' and apple.com/iphone-18-pro/specs is live; exact on-sale date not shown on those pages. Video specs essentially identical to iPhone 17 Pro except Cinematic mode up to 4K60 (17 Pro: 4K30) and a variable-aperture 48MP main camera. Apple support 109041 (en-us) still lists only 15/16/17 Pro for ProRes tables; an Apple iPhone User Guide version adds 18 Pro to 4K120 external ProRes (and a one-time 'Configure Pro Video Storage' step). Treat 18 Pro ProRes limits as same as 17 Pro.

cameras.name: DJI Inspire 3 (Zenmuse X9-8K Air)

codecs.name: CinemaDNG
codecs.ref: DJI Inspire 3 User Manual v3.0 (2024.09), Specifications > Recording Specifications table (values in MB/s = megabytes/s; x8 for Mb/s): CinemaDNG FF 4096x2160 25 fps = 221 MB/s = 1768 Mb/s; same ~8.0 bpp on all rows (e.g. 8192x4320 24 fps = 849 MB/s). Requires paid license. Manual's 3840x2160 75 fps cell reads '872MBps' (likely typo for ~622).

codecs.name: ProRes RAW (DJI high-rate tier, ~4 bpp)
codecs.ref: DJI Inspire 3 User Manual v3.0 (2024.09), Specifications > Recording Specifications table (values in MB/s = megabytes/s; x8 for Mb/s): ProRes RAW FF 4096x2160 25 fps = 111 MB/s = 888 Mb/s (~4.0 bpp; 8192x4320 24 fps = 425 MB/s same bpp). DJI's table labels the codec only 'ProRes RAW' (does not say RAW vs RAW HQ); ~4 bpp is above ProRes 422 HQ, consistent with Apple's RAW HQ range. Paid license.

codecs.name: ProRes RAW (DJI reduced-rate tier, ~2 bpp: 8K above 25 fps, 8K 2.39:1, 4K 120)
codecs.ref: DJI Inspire 3 User Manual v3.0 (2024.09), Specifications > Recording Specifications table (values in MB/s = megabytes/s; x8 for Mb/s): ProRes RAW FF 8192x4320 60 fps = 531 MB/s = 4248 Mb/s (~2.0 bpp). Table shows halved per-frame rate for 8K at 29.97-60 fps (e.g. 29.97 fps = 265 MB/s vs 24 fps = 425 MB/s), for 8K 2.39:1 at 72/75 fps (505/526 MB/s) and for 4K at 119.88/120 fps (265/249 MB/s). Column mapping inferred from the text-extracted table; values check out at constant bpp.

codecs.name: ProRes 422 HQ
codecs.ref: DJI Inspire 3 User Manual v3.0 (2024.09), Specifications > Recording Specifications table (values in MB/s = megabytes/s; x8 for Mb/s): ProRes 422 HQ FF 4096x2160 29.97 fps = 118 MB/s = 944 Mb/s (matches Apple WP 943 Mb/s). S35 4K modes max 60 fps. Manual's 7680x4320 25 fps cell reads 396 MB/s (likely typo; ~367 expected). No license needed.

cameras.name: DJI Inspire 2 + Zenmuse X7

codecs.name: CinemaDNG
codecs.ref: ESTIMATE (upper bound). X7 manual gives only 'maximum bitrate of 4.44 Gbps' for CinemaDNG/ProRes on CINESSD and no per-mode rates; bpp = 4.44e9/(6016*3200*30) at the top 6K 30 fps mode. 14-bit at 23.976, 12-bit otherwise. Lossless-compressed so real rate varies; at 23.976 14-bit the same cap would imply ~9.6 bpp. Requires Inspire 2 CinemaDNG license + CINESSD.

codecs.name: ProRes RAW
codecs.ref: ESTIMATE. Apple ProRes RAW White Paper (May 2023) gives no numeric table, only that ProRes RAW rates 'generally fall between' two ProRes flavors; midpoint of 147 and 220 Mb/s at 1920x1080 29.97 (ProRes WP April 2022) = 183.5 Mb/s. ProRes RAW is constant-quality, so real rates vary with detail/noise. X7 modes (manual v1.4): 6016x3200 / 5760x3240 up to 30 fps, 5440x2880 / 5120x2880 up to 24, 4096x2160 / 3840x2160 47.95/48 only. Requires DJI GO 4 update + license.

codecs.name: ProRes RAW HQ
codecs.ref: ESTIMATE. Apple ProRes RAW White Paper (May 2023) gives no numeric table, only that ProRes RAW HQ rates 'generally fall between' two ProRes flavors; midpoint of 220 and 330 Mb/s at 1920x1080 29.97 (ProRes WP April 2022) = 275.0 Mb/s. ProRes RAW is constant-quality, so real rates vary with detail/noise. X7 manual: RAW HQ only 6016x3200 and 5760x3240 at 23.976 fps.

codecs.name: ProRes 422 HQ
codecs.ref: Apple ProRes White Paper (April 2022), target data rate ProRes 422 HQ 1920x1080 29.97p = 220 Mb/s (bpp = Mbps*1e6/(1920*1080*29.97)). X7 manual: 5280x2160, 4096x2160, 3840x2160 up to 30 fps; 2704x1520, 2048x1080, 1920x1080 at 47.95-59.94 fps. Cross-check: Inspire 2 manual X5S spec lists 3840x2160 30p 422 HQ @900 Mb/s (WP: 884).

codecs.name: ProRes 4444 XQ
codecs.ref: Apple ProRes White Paper (April 2022), target data rate ProRes 4444 XQ 1920x1080 29.97p = 500 Mb/s (bpp = Mbps*1e6/(1920*1080*29.97)). X7 manual: 3840x2160 up to 30 fps; 2048x1080 and 1920x1080 at 47.95-59.94 fps. Cross-check: Inspire 2 X5S spec 3840x2160 30p 4444 XQ @2.0 Gb/s (WP: 1989).

cameras.notes: Source: Zenmuse X7 User Manual v1.4 (2018.07), Recording specifications. CINESSD codecs: CinemaDNG, ProRes RAW, ProRes RAW HQ, ProRes 422 HQ, ProRes 4444 XQ (require Inspire 2 license keys). MicroSD: H.264 (4096/3840/2720/1920 up to 59.94 fps; 3840x1572 up to 30) and H.265 (4096/3840/1920/2720/3840x1572 up to 30; 2720 and 1920 also 47.95/59.94). Manual lists H.264/H.265 frame rates as 23.976/24/29.97/30 and 47.95/59.94 (no 25/50). Max CINESSD bitrate 4.44 Gb/s. Higher-fps modes crop the sensor.
